flags.stderr:
-EXPERIMENTAL-xdp value
    	whether and how to use XDP. Can be one of: "off" (default), "ns", "redirect:<device name>", or "tunnel:<device name>"
  -EXPERIMENTAL-xdp-need-wakeup
    	EXPERIMENTAL. Use XDP_USE_NEED_WAKEUP with XDP sockets. (default true)
  -TESTONLY-afs-syscall-panic
    	TEST ONLY; do not ever use! Used for tests exercising gVisor panic reporting.
  -TESTONLY-autosave-image-path string
    	TEST ONLY; enable auto save for syscall tests and set path for state file.
  -TESTONLY-autosave-resume
    	TEST ONLY; enable auto save and resume for syscall tests and set path for state file.
  -TESTONLY-nftables
    	TEST ONLY; Enables nftables support in the sentry.
  -TESTONLY-test-name-env string
    	TEST ONLY; do not ever use! Used for automated tests to improve logging.
  -TESTONLY-unsafe-nonroot
    	TEST ONLY; do not ever use! This skips many security measures that isolate the host from the sandbox.
  -allow-connected-on-save
    	Allow network connections to stay established on save.
  -allow-flag-override
    	allow OCI annotations (dev.gvisor.flag.<name>) to override flags for debugging.
  -allow-live-tcp-migration
    	allow TCP connection state to be migrated. If false, connected TCP endpoints will be terminated during save/restore. (default true)
  -allow-packet-socket-write
    	allow writes on AF_PACKET sockets. When false, writes on AF_PACKET sockets will fail. When turned on, untrusted workloads may potentially attack the network because of the ability to craft arbitrary packets.
  -allow-rootfs-tar-annotation
    	allows the rootfs tar annotation to be set.
  -allow-suid
    	allows ID elevation when executing binaries with the SUID/SGID bits set. The OCI --no-new-privileges flag continues to prevent ID elevation even when this flag is true.
  -alsologtostderr
    	send log messages to stderr.
  -app-huge-pages
    	enable use of huge pages for application memory; requires /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/shmem_enabled = advise (default true)
  -boot-times-log string
    	if set, write the startup timeline of the sandbox to this file as JSON when the sandbox starts
  -buffer-pooling
    	DEPRECATED: this flag has no effect. (default true)
  -cgroupfs
    	DEPRECATED: this flag has no effect.
  -character-device-policy value
    	controls how character device files on gofer mounts (rootfs and bind mounts) are handled. 'emulated-only' serves devices implemented by the sentry and fails opens of other devices with ENXIO (default and more secure); 'prefer-emulated' serves sentry-implemented devices from the sentry and opens the rest through the host; 'passthrough' opens all of them through the host. Values: emulated-only|prefer-emulated|passthrough, default: emulated-only
  -control-rpc-stop-timeout duration
    	grace period given to in-flight RPCs on the sandbox control socket when the sandbox is shutting down. Once this timeout elapses, client connections are closed, and connections still processing an RPC are closed when their current RPC finishes. Set to 0 to close idle clients immediately. (default 15s)
  -coverage-fd int
    	file descriptor to write Go coverage output. (default -1)
  -coverage-report string
    	file path where Go coverage reports are written. Reports will only be generated if runsc is built with --collect_code_coverage and --instrumentation_filter Bazel flags.
  -cpu-num-from-quota
    	set cpu number to cpu quota (least integer greater or equal to quota value, but not less than 2) (default true)
  -dcache int
    	Set the global dentry cache size. This acts as a coarse-grained control on the number of host FDs simultaneously open by the sentry. If negative, per-mount caches are used. (default -1)
  -debug
    	enable debug logging.
  -debug-command string
    	comma-separated list of commands to be debugged if --debug-log is also set. Empty means debug all. "!" negates the expression. E.g. "create,start" or "!boot,events"
  -debug-log string
    	additional location for logs. If it ends with '/', log files are created inside the directory with default names. The following variables are available: %TIMESTAMP%, %COMMAND%.
  -debug-log-fd int
    	file descriptor to write debug logs to.  If set, the 'debug-log-dir' flag is ignored. (default -1)
  -debug-log-format string
    	log format: text (default), json, or json-k8s. (default "text")
  -debug-to-user-log
    	also emit Sentry logs to user-visible logs
  -directfs
    	directly access the container filesystems from the sentry. Sentry runs with higher privileges. (default true)
  -dump-goroutines-signal int
    	register signal handling that dumps all goroutine stacks. -1 disables it. (default -1)
  -enable-core-tags
    	enables core tagging. Requires host linux kernel >= 5.14.
  -fdlimit int
    	Specifies a limit on the number of host file descriptors that can be open. Applies separately to the sentry and gofer. Note: each file in the sandbox holds more than one host FD open. (default -1)
  -file-access value
    	specifies which filesystem validation to use for the root mount: exclusive (default), shared.
  -file-access-mounts value
    	specifies which filesystem validation to use for volumes other than the root mount: shared (default), exclusive. (default shared)
  -final-metrics-log string
    	if set, write all metric data to this file upon sandbox termination
  -fsgofer-host-uds
    	DEPRECATED: use host-uds=all
  -fuse
    	DEPRECATED: this flag has no effect. (default true)
  -gofer-network-namespace value
    	network namespace for gofers: null (default; an empty namespace shared by all gofers using the same --shared-root, which defaults to --root), new (a new empty namespace per gofer), host (the current namespace), or an absolute path to an existing namespace. (default null)
  -gso
    	enable host segmentation offload if it is supported by a network device. (default true)
  -gvisor-gro
    	enable gVisor generic receive offload
  -gvisor-marker-file
    	enable the presence of the /proc/gvisor/kernel_is_gvisor file that can be used by applications to detect that gVisor is in use
  -h	equivalent to the 'help' flag
  -help
    	show information about runsc subcommands and exit
  -host-fifo value
    	controls permission to access host FIFOs (or named pipes). Values: none|open, default: none
  -host-settings value
    	how to handle non-optimal host kernel settings: check (default, advisory-only), ignore (do not check), adjust (best-effort auto-adjustment), or enforce (auto-adjustment must succeed).
  -host-uds value
    	controls permission to access host Unix-domain sockets. Values: none|open|create|all, default: none
  -ignore-cgroups
    	don't configure cgroups.
  -in-sandbox-cgroup value
    	cgroup setup to use inside the sandbox: v1 (default), v2.
  -inode-numbers value
    	controls inode numbers on gofer mounts: 'passthrough' reports host inode numbers; 'virtual' assigns sandbox-private sequential numbers, which costs memory per file seen and a stat(2) per getdents(2) entry. Values: passthrough|virtual, default: passthrough
  -iouring
    	TEST ONLY; Enables io_uring syscalls in the sentry. Support is experimental and very limited.
  -kvm-use-cpu-nums
    	on KVM use vCPU numbers as CPU numbers in the sentry. This is necessary to support features like rseq.
  -lisafs
    	DEPRECATED: this flag has no effect. (default true)
  -log string
    	file path where internal debug information is written, default is stdout.
  -log-fd int
    	file descriptor to log to.  If set, the 'log' flag is ignored. (default -1)
  -log-format string
    	log format: text (default), json, or json-k8s. (default "text")
  -log-packets
    	enable network packet logging.
  -metric-server runsc metric-server
    	if set, export metrics on this address. This may either be 1) 'addr:port' to export metrics on a specific network interface address, 2) ':port' for exporting metrics on all interfaces, or 3) an absolute path to a Unix Domain Socket. The substring '%RUNTIME_ROOT%' will be replaced by the root directory. This flag must be specified in both runsc metric-server and `runsc create`, and their values must match.
  -mount-cgroup-v2
    	DEPRECATED: use in-sandbox-cgroup=v2
  -net-disconnect-ok
    	Indicates whether open network connections and open unix domain sockets should be disconnected upon save. (default true)
  -net-raw runsc exec
    	enable raw sockets. When false, raw sockets are disabled by removing CAP_NET_RAW from containers (runsc exec will still be able to utilize raw sockets). Raw sockets allow malicious containers to craft packets and potentially attack the network.
  -network value
    	specifies which network to use: sandbox (default), host, none. Using network inside the sandbox is more secure because it's isolated from the host network.
  -network-processors-per-channel int
    	number of goroutines in each channel for processng inbound packets. If 0, the link endpoint will divide GOMAXPROCS evenly among the number of channels specified by num-network-channels.
  -network-proxy-path string
    	EXPERIMENTAL. Path of an external SOCK_SEQPACKET Unix domain socket to attach the sandbox's primary network interface to, instead of an AF_PACKET socket.
  -num-network-channels int
    	number of underlying channels(FDs) to use for network link endpoints. (default 1)
  -nvproxy
    	LEGACY: enable support for Nvidia GPUs. GPU support gets automatically enabled if Nvidia devices are present in the OCI spec.
  -nvproxy-allow-unsupported-driver
    	allow nvproxy to be initialized with an unsupported driver version.
  -nvproxy-allowed-driver-capabilities string
    	Comma separated list of NVIDIA driver capabilities that are allowed to be requested by the container. If 'all' is specified here, it is resolved to all driver capabilities supported in nvproxy. If 'all' is requested by the container, it is resolved to this list. (default "utility,compute")
  -nvproxy-docker docker run --gpus
    	LEGACY: Injects nvidia-container-runtime-hook as a prestart hook. Try to use nvidia-container-runtime or docker run --gpus instead. Or manually add nvidia-container-runtime-hook as a prestart hook and set up NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES container environment variable.
  -nvproxy-driver-version string
    	NVIDIA driver ABI version to use. If empty, autodetect installed driver version. The special value 'latest' may also be used to use the latest ABI.
  -oci-seccomp
    	Enables loading OCI seccomp filters inside the sandbox.
  -overlay
    	DEPRECATED: use --overlay2=all:memory to achieve the same effect
  -overlay2 value
    	wrap mounts with overlayfs. Format is
    	* 'none' to turn overlay mode off
    	* {mount}:{medium}[,size={size}], where
    	    'mount' can be 'root' or 'all'
    	    'medium' can be 'memory', 'self' or 'dir=/abs/dir/path' in which filestore will be created
    	    'size' optional parameter overrides default overlay upper layer size
    	 (default root:self)
  -override-procs string
    	comma-separated list of proc files to override with stubs (e.g. kallsyms)
  -panic-log string
    	file path where panic reports and other Go's runtime messages are written.
  -panic-log-fd int
    	file descriptor to write Go's runtime messages. (default -1)
  -panic-signal int
    	register signal handling that panics. Usually set to SIGUSR2(12) to troubleshoot hangs. -1 disables it. (default -1)
  -pause-external-networking
    	Start the sandbox with external networking disabled. Only supported when using the sandbox network type. The network can be unpaused manually after the sandbox is running.
  -pcap-log string
    	location of PCAP log file.
  -platform string
    	specifies which platform to use: systrap (default), ptrace, kvm, auto. auto picks the best platform usable on the host. (default "systrap")
  -platform_device_path string
    	path to a platform-specific device file (e.g. /dev/kvm for KVM platform), or comma-separated platform=path pairs (e.g. kvm=/dev/kvm2) that apply only to the named platforms. If unset, will use a sane platform-specific default. --platform=auto accepts only platform=path pairs.
  -pod-init-config string
    	path to configuration file with additional steps to take during pod creation.
  -profile
    	prepares the sandbox to use Golang profiler. Note that enabling profiler loosens the seccomp protection added to the sandbox (DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION).
  -profile-block string
    	collects a block profile to this file path for the duration of the container execution. Requires -profile=true.
  -profile-cpu string
    	collects a CPU profile to this file path for the duration of the container execution. Requires -profile=true.
  -profile-gc-interval duration
    	forces a garbage collection cycle every this duration while another type of time-based profiling is enabled. Requires -profile=true.
  -profile-heap string
    	collects a heap profile to this file path for the duration of the container execution. Requires -profile=true.
  -profile-mutex string
    	collects a mutex profile to this file path for the duration of the container execution. Requires -profile=true.
  -profiling-metrics string
    	comma separated list of metric names which are going to be written to the profiling-metrics-log file from within the sentry in CSV format. profiling-metrics will be snapshotted at a rate specified by profiling-metrics-rate-us. Requires profiling-metrics-log to be set. (DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION).
  -profiling-metrics-log string
    	file name to use for profiling-metrics output; use the special value '-' to write to the user-visible logs. (DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION)
  -profiling-metrics-rate-us int
    	the target rate (in microseconds) at which profiling metrics will be snapshotted. (default 1000)
  -qdisc value
    	specifies which queueing discipline to apply by default to the non loopback nics used by the sandbox. (default fifo)
  -qdisc-tbf-burst uint
    	bucket depth in bytes when --qdisc=tbf.
  -qdisc-tbf-rate uint
    	egress rate limit in bytes/sec when --qdisc=tbf.
  -rdmaproxy
    	WIP: enable RDMA support for containers with /dev/infiniband/uverbs* devices.
  -ref-leak-mode value
    	sets reference leak check mode: disabled (default), log-names, log-traces.
  -reproduce-nat
    	Scrape the host netns NAT table and reproduce it in the sandbox.
  -reproduce-nftables
    	Attempt to scrape and reproduce nftable rules inside the sandbox. Overrides reproduce-nat when true.
  -restore-spec-validation value
    	how to handle spec validation during restore. (default enforce)
  -root string
    	root directory for storage of container state, defaults are $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/runsc, /var/run/runsc.
  -rootless
    	it allows the sandbox to be started with a user that is not root. Sandbox and Gofer processes may run with same privileges as current user.
  -rx-checksum-offload
    	enable RX checksum offload. (default true)
  -sandbox-creation-cpu-policy value
    	CPU limit applied during sandbox creation and initialization, until the application starts. Takes the same values, and applies under the same conditions, as --sandbox-lifecycle-cpu-policy. Note that pre-cgroup-setup sandbox creation steps are not CPU-limited regardless of this flag's value. If you need to limit end-to-end sandbox creation, run gVisor in a CPU-limited cgroup. (default uncapped)
  -sandbox-lifecycle-cpu-policy linux.resources.cpu.quota
    	CPU limit of non-creation sandbox lifecycle operations: checkpoint, restore, and teardown (while the application is not running). Values: 'uncapped', '<N>m' (thousandths of a CPU, e.g. 2500m), '<N>x' (multiple of the OCI spec limit, e.g. 3.5x), or 'max(<value>,...)' for the largest of several values. 1x naturally means the OCI-spec-provided limit, and the limit never goes below it. Only applies when the OCI spec sets a CPU quota (linux.resources.cpu.quota, or `cpu.max` in `linux.resources.unified`), and only when `runsc` creates the sandbox cgroup itself; never to pods or pre-existing cgroups. (default max(4x,1000m))
  -save-restore-netstack
    	DEPRECATED: this flag has no effect. (default true)
  -shared-root string
    	directory for storage of state shared across sandboxes on the system. Defaults to the value of --root. Point this at a shared system-wide directory if --root is not reused across sandboxes. Access to --shared-root allows identification of running sandboxes, but not control over them.
  -sidecar-release-enforcement-policy value
    	when spawned sidecar binaries must match runsc's release: NEVER, ALWAYS, or IF_RELEASE_BUILD. May be overridden by setting GVISOR_ENFORCE_RELEASE=SKIP as env var. (default IF_RELEASE_BUILD)
  -sidecar-usage-policy gvisor-bin
    	DEPRECATED: this flag has no effect; sidecar binaries must always be installed in gvisor-bin (or `GVISOR_SIDECAR_BINARIES_DIR`). (default DEFAULT)
  -signal-unkillable-policy value
    	controls protection of PID namespace init processes from signals under Linux SIGNAL_UNKILLABLE semantics: none (default) or linux.
  -software-gso
    	enable gVisor segmentation offload when host offload can't be enabled. (default true)
  -state-engine value
    	selects the state serialization engine used when saving checkpoints: graph (default) or wire.
  -strace
    	enable strace.
  -strace-event
    	send strace to event.
  -strace-log-size uint
    	default size (in bytes) to log data argument blobs. (default 1024)
  -strace-syscalls string
    	comma-separated list of syscalls to trace. If --strace is true and this list is empty, then all syscalls will be traced.
  -systemd-cgroup
    	EXPERIMENTAL. Use systemd for cgroups.
  -systrap-disable-fast-path
    	unconditionally disables the Systrap fast path.
  -systrap-disable-syscall-patching
    	disables syscall patching when using the Systrap platform. May be necessary to use in case the workload uses the GS register, or uses ptrace within gVisor. Has significant performance implications and is only recommended when the sandbox is known to run otherwise-incompatible workloads. Only relevant for x86.
  -tpuproxy
    	LEGACY: enable support for TPU devices. TPU support gets automatically enabled if TPU devices are present in the OCI spec.
  -trace string
    	collects a Go runtime execution trace to this file path for the duration of the container execution.
  -traceback string
    	golang runtime's traceback level (default "system")
  -tx-checksum-offload
    	enable TX checksum offload.
  -version
    	show version and exit.
  -vfs2
    	DEPRECATED: this flag has no effect. (default true)
  -watchdog-action string
    	sets what action the watchdog takes when triggered: log (default), panic. (default "log")
